segments.heading: What are we testing?
segments.body: If joint-state feedback disappears during motion, does the supervisor detect it, block new commands, and recover without replaying old intent?
segments.proof: The injected fault is feedback delivery at the consumer. The simulator remains running.

segments.heading: 1 / Motion and feedback
segments.body: Begin a six-second move toward A. Joint feedback is arriving and the supervisor is EXECUTING.
segments.proof: The arm is moving; feedback age is normally close to zero.

segments.heading: 2 / Interrupt feedback
segments.body: Stop delivering joint-state samples to the supervisor. Physics and the controller continue. The displayed last-received joint values now freeze.
segments.proof: Watch feedback age rise past the 0.50 wall-second watchdog limit.

segments.heading: 2 / Interrupt feedback
segments.body: Stop delivering joint-state samples to the supervisor. Physics and the controller continue. The displayed last-received joint values now freeze.
segments.proof: Watch feedback age rise past the 0.50 wall-second watchdog limit.

segments.heading: 3 / Detect and latch FAULT
segments.body: About 0.52 wall seconds after injection, the supervisor reports STALE_FEEDBACK and requests cancellation. The recorded controller acknowledges cancellation.
segments.proof: Cancellation permits controller deceleration. It is not proof of an instantaneous or certified physical stop.

segments.heading: 3 / Detect and latch FAULT
segments.body: About 0.52 wall seconds after injection, the supervisor reports STALE_FEEDBACK and requests cancellation. The recorded controller acknowledges cancellation.
segments.proof: Cancellation permits controller deceleration. It is not proof of an instantaneous or certified physical stop.

segments.heading: 4 / Reject new intent
segments.body: A new move request is deliberately attempted. The supervisor rejects it because the fault is latched. This is a software decision: no new motion should appear.
segments.proof: Clearing the last error message alone does not re-enable commands.

segments.heading: 5 / Restore; explicitly recover
segments.body: Restore sample delivery and call recover(). It requires a running controller, fresh advancing feedback, and low velocity over a settling interval.
segments.proof: Recovery re-establishes readiness; it does not resume unfinished A.

segments.heading: 6 / Send a fresh goal B
segments.body: After recovery succeeds, submit B as new intent. This is a different target from the interrupted A. Watch the arm move again.

segments.heading: Result / Recovery verified
segments.body: The fresh command reaches B and passes measured completion checks. The sequence is: detect, latch, reject, restore, recover, then execute new intent.
segments.proof: Recorded outcomes: interrupted A = FAULT (STALE_FEEDBACK); fresh B = SUCCEEDED.
